author: Akira YUYAMA

relations.subject: Antoine Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
relations.evidence: Antoine Isaac Silvestre de Sacy (1758-1838), who became the founding president of the Société Asiatique in 1822 until 1829.

relations.subject: Jean Pierre Abel-Rémusat
relations.evidence: His Secretary to the Society, Jean Pierre Abel-Rémusat (1788-1832), succeeded to the presidency in 1829 until his premature death from cholera in June 1832.

relations.subject: Eugène Burnouf
relations.evidence: In the meantime Eugène Burnouf was elected “Secrétaire-adjoint”, more precisely on 27 April 1826.

relations.subject: Antoine Isaac Silvestre de Sacy
relations.evidence: Silvestre de Sacy had to resume its presidency in August 1832 after the sudden death of Abel-Rémusat. He served the Society for the next two years until 1834

relations.subject: Eugène Burnouf
relations.evidence: Eugène Burnouf was then appointed to be Secretary on 3 September 1832.

relations.subject: Amédée Jaubert
relations.evidence: In any case Amédée Jaubert was elected to be next president (1834-1847)

relations.subject: Joseph Toussain Reinaud
relations.evidence: Joseph Toussain Reinaud (1795-1867) succeeded Jaubert for the period of 1847 to 1867.

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: Julius von (or Jules) Mohl (1800-1876) served the Society as “Secrétaire-adjoint” from 1840, and “Secrétaire” from 1852

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: and “Secrétaire” from 1852 when Eugène Burnouf died at an early age

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: Julius himself studied theology in Tübingen, and became more interested in Oriental studies.

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: He decided to go to Paris, where he pursued Persian with Silvestre de Sacy and Sinology with Abel-Rémusat.

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: He decided to go to Paris, where he pursued Persian with Silvestre de Sacy and Sinology with Abel-Rémusat.

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: In 1826 the State Government of Württemberg appointed him to professorship in Oriental languages in his alma mater. He held the position for seven years

relations.subject: Julius von Mohl
relations.evidence: appointed to professor of Persian at the Collège de France in 1847. He actually took this appointment in 1847 and occupied it until his death in 1876.

relations.subject: Joseph Ernest Renan
relations.evidence: had taught Renan Sanskrit at the Collège de France, had befriended him and guided him personally in the early stages of his career.

relations.subject: Georg Heinrich August Ewald
relations.evidence: Being a professor of Semitic studies at Göttingen... seven professors gave up their positions on 18 November 1837.

relations.subject: Georg Heinrich August Ewald
relations.evidence: Heinrich Ewald felt impelled to leave Göttingen to take up an appointment at the University of Tübingen from 1838 to 1848.

relations.subject: Georg Heinrich August Ewald
relations.evidence: He returned to Göttingen in 1848 to resume his professorship and resigned again in 1867 for political reasons.

relations.subject: Georg Heinrich August Ewald
relations.evidence: Heinrich Ewald and Christian Lassen were a good combination to work for unity in Oriental studies in Germany. It was a boon to German Orientalists to see the launching of the new periodical as a result of their cooperation in 1837.

relations.subject: Friedrich Rückert
relations.evidence: Friedrich Rückert (1788-1866), Professor of Oriental Studies at Erlangen
